chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Abī 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The one performing tamattu' has mut'ah available to him until the sun passes the meridian on the Day of 'Arafah, and he has hajj available to him until the sun passes the meridian on the Day of al-Nahr.

key_terms.الْحَجُّ: the hajj rite in this legal context
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: the tamattu' rite or state associated with this form of hajj
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun's decline from the meridian, i.e. midday passing
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice, the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: Until what time can a pilgrim still catch tamattu' and hajj according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal time limits related to tamattu' and hajj rites. It defines until when a person may still be considered to catch the opportunity for mut'ah and until when he may still catch the hajj.
